meta.teaser: Tennis started as a hand game in France, long before rackets existed.

page.title: Before rackets, players hit the ball with their bare hands
page.sub: The story of how tennis was born
page.bigIdea: Your sport is about 900 years old. It grew from a French hand game into lawn tennis, one small change at a time.

cards.title: The game of the palm
cards.front: The first tennis players had no rackets at all.
cards.back: In 12th-century northern France, people hit the ball with their palm. The game was called jeu de paume, which means "game of the palm".
cards.tryit: Rally a soft ball against a wall using only your hand. Count how long you last.

cards.title: From gloves to rackets
cards.front: Hands hurt, so players kept upgrading their gear.
cards.back: Bare hands gave way to gloves. By the 16th century, the glove had become a racket. The game moved into closed courts with walls.
cards.tryit: Hit 10 balls with your hand, then 10 with your racket. Notice the difference.

cards.title: The sport of kings
cards.front: Royals loved this game, and one word came from them.
cards.back: King Henry VIII built a court at Hampton Court Palace in 1530. Servers shouted "Tenez!", meaning "Receive!" That call probably gave tennis its name.
cards.tryit: Before your next serve in practice, say "Tenez!" quietly. Feel like a king.

cards.title: Tennis moves onto grass
cards.front: In the 1800s, people took the game outside.
cards.back: Harry Gem and Augurio Perera played on a croquet lawn in Birmingham. In 1874, Walter Wingfield sold boxed sets of his game, with an hourglass-shaped court.
cards.tryit: Sketch an hourglass court next to a modern court. Which would be harder to play on?

cards.title: The very first Wimbledon
cards.front: Today it's huge. In 1877, it was tiny.
cards.back: Just 22 men entered the first Wimbledon in 1877. Spencer Gore won. About 200 people watched the final, with flannel-covered rubber balls.
cards.tryit: Look up how many people watch a Wimbledon final today. Compare it with 200.

words.d: French for "game of the palm", the hand game before tennis.
The old indoor version with walls, still played today.
Tennis played outdoors on grass, invented in the 1870s.

quiz.q: What did the very first tennis players hit the ball with?
quiz.hint: Think about what "jeu de paume" means.
quiz.why: Jeu de paume means "game of the palm", because players used their hands.

quiz.q: Where does the word "tennis" probably come from?
opts: The name of an English town
quiz.hint: Look at card 3. What did servers call out?
quiz.why: Servers called "Tenez!" to warn the other player, and the word stuck.

quiz.q: Why did tennis change from hands to gloves to rackets?
opts: Players wanted better gear to play better and hurt less
quiz.hint: Think about why you upgrade your own racket or strings.
quiz.why: Each change made the game easier on the hand and more fun to play.

quiz.q: What was the first Wimbledon in 1877 like?
opts: Small, with 22 players and about 200 fans at the final
quiz.why: Wimbledon started tiny and grew over 150 years into a giant event.

page.think: Tennis changed many times: hands, gloves, rackets, grass, new rules. If you could add one new rule or gadget to tennis today, what would it be, and why?
